script.title: How Indie Artists Beat Bollywood's Music Monopoly #shorts

segments.text: Bollywood no longer controls what music you listen to.
segments.broll: young man wearing headphones dark room
broll_alt: listening to music on smartphone close up
sound mixing audio studio close up

segments.text: India's music economy just touched 1.8 billion dollars, according to a recent report.
And a massive 43 percent of all streams now belong to independent artists.
segments.broll: close up hands playing acoustic guitar

segments.text: Earlier, massive film studios decided who got heard and kept most of the profits.
segments.broll: vintage cinema projector spinning dark room
broll_alt: empty movie theater hall wide shot
retro record player needle spinning vinyl

segments.text: Now, audio streaming apps allow creators to publish directly without big labels.
broll_alt: hand holding mobile phone night light
person typing laptop keyboard close up

segments.text: Instead of film budgets, musicians now earn directly every time you play their track.
segments.broll: steaming indian chai cup street stall
broll_alt: pouring hot tea into glass slow motion

script.description: Discover how independent music creators are breaking Bollywood's traditional monopoly in India's massive music economy. Learn how streaming apps helped indie artists claim 43% of total streams. Educational breakdown of India's changing music business. #IndieMusic #MusicBusiness #PaisaDecoded

facts_to_verify.claim: India's music economy reached $1.8 billion according to EY report
Independent music claims 43% of total streams in India

script.chosen_candidate: India’s Music Economy Hits $1.8 Billion as Independent Music Claims 43% of Streams, EY Report Finds - Yahoo Finance
script.why_it_will_work: It taps into the massive cultural shift among young Indians consuming non-Bollywood indie music on Spotify, revealing the eye-opening revenue numbers behind their everyday listening habits.
